label: no
controls_available: Three fixed views: door, desk, and cabinet.
Simplified TURN LEFT and TURN RIGHT buttons navigate the views.
Visible scene hotspot clicks reveal the label, collect the empty frame, open the lens drawer, collect the lens, and use the completed loupe on the label; the door handle is the final exit control.
Select a tray object and then click a second tray object to combine them, or click a visible scene destination to use the selected object.
One three-digit digit ward with digit-wheel buttons and SET DIAL; the ward seizes after three wrong entries.
Runner settings are observation_window_ms=0, frames_per_observation=1, and play_time_seconds=240.
autonomous_processes: No outcome-affecting autonomous task-state process occurs before terminal submission: the mechanic registers no task timer, interval, physics update, motion loop, or random update.
Scene, inventory, combination, and lock state changes happen synchronously in response to the agent's input and immediately rerender.

After the successful door click, the CSS vault-door transform transitions for 0.8 seconds while the result is submitted; this is post-outcome presentation and cannot change the available action opportunity.
A result response after a failed three-strike submission can install a fresh state, but that reset follows the agent's submission action and is not autonomous evolution during an active delay.
grouped_control_modes: scene_click: visible room-object and final door-handle clicks
inventory_select_pair: select two tray cards to combine
inventory_select_scene: select a tray card and click a scene destination
digit_controls: open the digit ward, increment digit wheels, and submit SET DIAL

clause_i.reason: For the candidate digit-controls mode, the required three-digit answer is a seed-dependent static clue revealed on the desk. Prior actions and task times alone do not contain the observed digits, so no observation-free q can choose the optimal digit submission across generated seeds.

clause_ii.reason: Under the configured zero-millisecond observation window, the current door frame shows the digit ward but not the previously revealed desk inscription. A bounded recent window therefore cannot supply the static clue; a normal solution must retain it across view changes. This is a memory limitation, not evidence of a changing task state.

clause_iii.reason: No legitimate grouped control mode has an autonomous state change H_t to H_t^tau for 0 < tau < Delta while success remains possible. Waiting leaves the views, targets, flags, inventory, clue, and digit-entry value unchanged, so no available action loses value or advantage. The only visible transition is the post-success door animation.

common_visible_process: None. Before terminal submission, the visible world changes only after an agent click or selection; the post-success door transition is outside the active outcome opportunity.

pre_run.reason: The source has no autonomous outcome phase: success is reached through discrete input-triggered state changes, and the final result submission is administrative. No pre-run percentage is defined, and this cannot alter the mathematical No from clause (iii).

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 selects three views, only the digit lock, a three-digit clue, no colour lock, no hook chain, no decoys, clear cues, and three allowed wrong entries.
The simplified surface uses turn buttons plus select-then-click object interactions; the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame and a 240-second play allowance.
The runner repeats the zero-millisecond, one-frame observation settings and marks the task synchronous.
The controlled difficulty parameters are copied into generation; the seed is used to create a fixed challenge and static digit answer, with no task-time update.
The level-1 topology has door/desk/cabinet and only the label, frame, lens drawer, lens, and loupe path; colour and key targets and the second recipe are gated off by the inactive parameters.
The browser reads the selected interaction mode, renders simplified turn buttons, and changes view state only in the synchronous navigate handler.
Scene discoveries, item combination, and item use mutate flags/inventory immediately and rerender; no autonomous update is scheduled.
The digit wheel and SET DIAL are ordinary click handlers, and simplified tray selection dispatches only select-pair or select-scene actions.
The only asynchronous fetch is result handling after completion or seizure; rendering initializes a static local model and contains no timer or animation loop.
The sole task-specific transition is the 0.8-second vault-door transform applied after the door is marked open.

The grader replays a finite ordered event transcript from an initial state, checks synchronous control sources and lock answers, and computes the terminal result without timestamps or elapsed-time state.
The verifier only loads the exported result and delegates to the independent grader.
The visible solver performs the clue/object sequence with clicks and selection, submits the digit answer, and waits only for the terminal pass indicator; it has no timed or motion-dependent action.
